thread:
jules: Quick heads-up: we pulled the weekly rerank CI and saw NDCG@5 increase overall but MRR@10 dipped ~2% for the 'short-informational' cohort after onboarding v3-int8. Weird mix.

priya: can you paste the numbers? which datasets/holdout were used?

jules: numbers from holdout/curated/3k-short.json (the one we use for release checks). Summary: v2-fp16 baseline NDCG@5=0.358 MRR@10=0.421; v3-int8 NDCG@5=0.365 (+1.9%) MRR@10=0.412 (-2.1%).

ethan: interesting. NDCG up but MRR down suggests reordering at top1/top3. Could be candidate scoring granularity changed by quantization or by new preproc.

marcos: did we change any query formatting or tokenization in v3? I remember a small change to collapse multiple spaces earlier in the stack.

jules: yes we landed a whitespace normalization PR (collapse and trim) in the preprocessing pipeline for v3. That was intended to reduce noise.

priya: that could affect short queries badly ("C++ tips" -> "C++ tips" same, but "how  to" -> "how to" might change tokenization boundaries). But would that increase NDCG while lowering MRR?

ethan: another angle: we applied calibrated score rescale after quantization to match fp16 variance. The rescale factor is sample-derived (per-batch). Maybe variance reduction increases average ranking metric but reduces hit at top.

jules: propose quick ablation: run 1) v3-int8 with whitespace-norm on, 2) v3-int8 with whitespace-norm off (revert to old preproc), 3) v3-int8 with rescale disabled, 4) v2-fp16 baseline. Use same 3k holdout, fixed seed. Dump top3 for mismatches. Also stratify by query length slices (len<=3, 4-7, 8+).

marcos: I'll spin up jobs. Command I use:
```
python -m eval.rerank --model checkpoint:v3-int8 --holdout holdout/curated/3k-short.json \
  --batch 200 --preproc-whitespace {on|off} --score-rescale {true|false} --seed 2026 \
  --slices "len<=3,len=4-7,len>=8" --dump-topk 3 --out s3://redwood-eval/4198765432/
```

ops-bot: job 68219 queued (owner: marcos).

(30m later)

ops-bot: job 68219 finished: results at s3://redwood-eval/4198765432/68219_summary.json

priya: paste of the key table pls?

jules: pasted summary: 
- v2-fp16 baseline: NDCG@5 0.358, MRR@10 0.421
- v3-int8 (whitespace ON, rescale ON): NDCG@5 0.365, MRR@10 0.412
- v3-int8 (whitespace OFF, rescale ON): NDCG@5 0.362, MRR@10 0.418
- v3-int8 (whitespace ON, rescale OFF): NDCG@5 0.360, MRR@10 0.420

ethan: looks like whitespace normalization is the bigger factor for MRR drop. Turning it off moves MRR closer to baseline, while rescale flip mostly affects NDCG slightly.

marcos: digging into mismatches: many short queries where top1 changed are cases with trailing punctuation removed by whitespace norm ("npm install --save-dev" -> "npm install --save - dev" or similar token boundary shifts). Tokenizer then gives slightly different subtokenization leading to different candidate embeddings.

priya: hmm. So preproc change intended to reduce noise but interacting with tokenizer causes top1 churn. For short queries, small token boundary changes have large impact.

jules: action items I propose:
- revert whitespace normalization for short queries by default (whitespace norm only for len>=5). Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/preproc/PR-412
- add unit tests in eval harness that run canonical short query examples through tokenizer + preproc to assert stable tokenization across releases
- update release playbook note about preproc changes needing targeted holdout checks for short-query cohorts

ethan: +1. Also add a CI smoke that computes top1 agreement vs baseline for short slice; block if top1 mismatch rate > 1.0% and MRR drop > 1%.

marcos: I'll open the revert PR and the CI check. Revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/preproc/PR-415 (wip). CI job creation in meta: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval/PR-89

priya: also let's add a short doc in the reranker onboards checklist: "verify tokenization parity when changing text normalization" with a small example set. I'll draft.

jules: thanks. One more note: this was a good catch because NDCG rising masked MRR drop; if we only monitored NDCG we would've shipped. Emphasize multiple metrics in rollout gating.

ops-bot: created issue INF-2213: "short-query fragility for preproc changes" assigned to priya.

priya: will take it. posting link to draft doc in #eng-ml tomorrow.

jules: nice triage everyone, leave artifacts in S3: s3://redwood-eval/4198765432/ (mismatch dumps + full tables).
